modules.module_title: Collection and preparation of raw materials and tools

pcs.pc_description: Gather raw materials such as coconuts and husk for coir fibre production.
Gather traditional tools, such as iron rods and hand-beaters, as well as modern machines such as Dehusking machines, Defibering machines, and Refining machines.
Organise and arrange raw materials and tools at the workplace, ensuring accessibility and safety.
Transport any extra materials to the designated storage area to maintain workplace order.

modules.module_title: Coir fibre extraction using traditional methods

pcs.pc_description: Dry coconut shells under sunlight for several days to aid in husk separation.
Soak dried coconut shells in water for over six months to soften the husk.
Remove the coconuts from the water and repeatedly beat them with an iron rod to remove the fibres.
Manually peel off the outer layer to separate the husk.
Bundle the husk and soak it again for further softening.
Use husk bundles in a water tank for two to four days for refinement.
Extract fibres by manually beating the soaked husk or using traditional tools.

modules.module_title: Coir fibre extraction using modern machines

pcs.pc_description: Put the dried coconut shells into a Dehusking machine to separate the husk.
Transfer the husk to a Defibering machine to break it down into finer fibres.
Use a refining machine, locally known as 'kudu,' to remove unwanted particles and extract clean coir fibres.
Roll the refined fibres into bundles for easy handling and transportation.

modules.module_title: Spinning and Twisting of Coir fibre

pcs.pc_description: Strengthen fibres by twisting two strands together using a traditional spinning wheel or a mechanised spinning machine.
Extend the fibre length by joining twine ends through friction or using a mechanised splicing tool.
Bundle the spun coir fibres and prepare large spools for further product manufacturing.
Regularly clean traditional tools such as iron rods and hand-beaters to prevent rusting.
Perform routine checks on modern machines such as Dehusking and Defibering machines to ensure optimal performance.

Follow safety protocols, such as wearing protective gear and ensuring proper machine handling practices.

pcs.pc_description: Select coir fibres based on the product type, ensuring suitable colour, texture, and durability.
Clean the fibres to remove impurities and unwanted remains and Soften the fibres through soaking and proper drying to improve flexibility.
Separate fibres into uniform strands for consistency in product production.
Spin coir fibres into yarn using a traditional hand spindle or mechanised spinning wheel. Make sure that even twisting and tension while spinning to create a strong, uniform thread.
Test yarn strength and elasticity to ensure durability for different product applications. Wind the finished yarn into spools for quick handling during product construction.
Select the appropriate weaving technique (handloom, power loom, or manual braiding) based on product design.
Set up the loom or workstation, ensuring that the fibres and tools are properly connected. Interlace coir fibres are designed to create even, tight weaves, ensuring strength and durability.
Maintain tension across the weave to prevent sagging or loose areas. Examine the weave periodically to ensure uniformity and address any irregularities.
Measure and cut coir yarn to the required dimensions for specific products (e.g., mats, ropes, decors).
Create product components by binding, stitching, or knotting fibres securely.
Shape the product according to the design, using moulds or frames if required.
Enhance high-stress areas with additional fibre layers to enhance durability.
Maintain structural stability by securing joints and tightening weaves.

modules.module_title: Product Specification in Coir Product Making

pcs.pc_description: Home décor making in coir involves crafting items like planters, show piece, wall hangings, etc. by shaping quality fibres, adding decorative touches, and ensuring durability.
Coir doormat making involves selecting sturdy fibres, weaving them into a tight, durable mat, adding patterns or borders, and ensuring quality for long-lasting use.
Coir rope weaving involves twisting strong fibres into sturdy strands, providing uniform thickness and durability for various applications.
Coir brush making involves bundling stiff fibres, securing them to a handle, trimming for uniformity, and ensuring durability for effective cleaning.
Trim excess fibres and smooth out rough edges for a polished finish.
Include decorative elements such as coloured fibres, patterns, or embellishments as per product design.
Apply protective treatments (natural oils, waterproof coatings) to increase product longevity.
Verify that the product design is aligned with customer preferences and market demands.
Examine the product for uniformity in weave, strength, and overall craftsmanship.
Test the product's durability, load capacity, or flexibility, depending on its intended purpose. Remove any loose fibres, uneven knots, or other defects.
Perform a final quality inspection, ensuring the product meets established standards before packaging.
Clean tools such as spindles, looms, cutting shears, and moulds after each use to eliminate coir dust and fibres.
Inspect tools regularly for wear and damage, ensuring smooth operation and safety.
Lubricate rotating parts of spinning wheels and looms to maintain efficiency.
Sharpen cutting tools and replace worn-out components to ensure accurate cutting and shaping.
Store tools in a dry area to prevent rust and damage.
Maintain records of maintenance activities and replace tools as necessary to avoid production delays.
